rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion For Protective Order; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities; Declaration Of Counsel
rulings.Rulings: This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Russell S. Roeca. Before the court is Trustee and Respondent Jon Vigna's Notice of Motion and Motion for Protective Order ("Motion") filed on May 4, 2026. Hearing on Trustee and Respondent Jon Vigna's Motion to Dismiss Remaining Claims in Petitioners' May 13, 2026 [sic] Petition, for Lack of Standing, or in the Alternative, to Strike Those Portions Which Petitioners Lack Standing is set concurrently with this Motion. On May 13, 2025, Petitioners filed Petition For: (1) Relief Under Probate Code Section 850; (2) Order Directing Trustee; and (3) An Accounting ("Petition"). The Petition's First Cause of Action, brought under Probate Code sec. 850, was settled and order approving the settlement was entered June 17, 2026. Dismissal with Prejudice of the First Cause of Action was filed June 29, 2026. On March 3, 2026, Petitioners propounded on Respondent discovery related to the remaining causes of action. Per the Notice of Motion and Motion, Movant seeks an order pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure sections 2017.020, 2019.030, 2030.090, 2031.060, and 2033.080 for a protective order staying all pending written discovery and pending discovery motions until Petitioners establish their standing to bring the remaining claims in the Petition. For the reasons articulated in the concurrently-issued tentative ruling on the concurrently-set Motion to Dismiss, the Motion is DENIED. Any party wishing to contest this tentative ruling by appearing at the scheduled hearing must so advise other parties and the courtroom clerk (415-551-3702) no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day before the hearing. rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE GAETANO (THOMAS) IVELI REVOCABLE TRUST, DATED 12/9/02
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Dismiss Remaining Claims In Petitioners May 13, 2026 Petition For Lack Of Standing Or, In The Alternative, To Strike Those Portions Which Petitioners Lack Standing; Memorandum Of Points And Authoritiies; Declaration Of Counsel
rulings.Rulings: [Part 1 of 3] This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Russell S. Roeca. Before the court is Trustee and Respondent Jon Vigna's Motion to Dismiss Remaining Claims in Petitioners' May 13, 2026 [sic] Petition, for Lack of Standing, or in the Alternative, to Strike Those Portions Which Petitioners Lack Standing ("Motion") filed on May 4, 2026. On May 13, 2025, Petitioners filed Petition For: (1) Relief Under Probate Code Section 850; (2) Order Directing Trustee; and (3) An Accounting, ("Petition"). The Petition's First Cause of Action, brought under Probate Code sec. 850, was settled and order approving the settlement was entered June 17, 2026. Dismissal with Prejudice of the First Cause of Action was filed June 29, 2026. The Petition's remaining causes of action are: (1) "Second Cause Of Action For An Order Instructing The Trustee (Against Respondent As Trustee Of Tom's Trust)" brought in Petitioners' capacity as "judgment creditors of Tom's Estate and Trust" and "the Estate's sole remaining creditor" (pars. 143, 148) and under the Trust's language that the Trustee pay "legally enforceable claims against the Grantor or the Grantor's estate" (par. 144). This cause of action seeks court determination of creditor priority and initiation of disbursements, and payment to Petitioners (par. 149); and (2) "Third Cause Of Action For An Accounting (Against Respondent As Trustee Of Tom's Trust)," seeking an order compelling a trust accounting for the period of Mr. Vigna's administration of the Trust, from December 2, 2019 through present, specifically as to allocation and payment of attorneys' fees between administration of the Trust and the Estate, and providing a copy to Petitioners. On March 3, 2026, Petitioners propounded on Respondent discovery related to the remaining causes of action. Per the Amended Notice of Motion, Movant argues Petitioners' remaining claims should be dismissed under Probate Code sec. 17202, as they are bringing an action concerning the internal affairs of the Trust by requesting an accounting be ordered and are neither beneficiaries nor trustees of the Trust, but only creditors who are specifically denied standing under Probate Code section 17200(b)(2), or in the alternative, the court should strike issues Petitioners lack standing to pursue, citing Code of Civil Procedure section 436. The Motion is DENIED. Overall, the Motion has not convinced the court to dismiss the Petition's remaining causes of action, on any authority offered in the Motion.

rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE GAETANO (THOMAS) IVELI REVOCABLE TRUST, DATED 12/9/02
rulings.Calendar Matter: ADDED TO CALENDAR FOR Notice Of Motion And Motion To Dismiss Remaining Claims In Petitioners May 13, 2026 Petition For Lack Of Standing Or, In The Alternative, To Strike Those Portions Which Petitioners Lack Standing (Added For Posting Of Tentative Ruling)
rulings.Rulings: [Part 2 of 3] Insofar as the Motion is bought pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure sections 435 and 436 to strike certain portions of the Petition, it is untimely (See, sec. 435(b)(1), "(b)(1) Any party, within the time allowed to respond to a pleading may serve and file a notice of motion to strike the whole or any part thereof, but this time limitation shall not apply to motions specified in subdivision (e) [motion for judgment on the pleadings under Section 438(i)(1)]."). Respondent filed Response To Petition For Relief Under Probate Code [sec.]850; For Order Directing Trustee; For An Accounting, on July 11, 2025. Insofar as the Motion asks the court, in its discretion under Section 436, to "Strike out any irrelevant, false, or improper matter inserted in any pleading. [or] Strike out all or any part of any pleading not drawn or filed in conformity with the laws of this state, a court rule, or an order of the court," the court declines to do so, at this time, on the basis of the showing in this Motion. Insofar as the Motion is brought pursuant to Probate Code sections 17200, 15642, 16060-16064, and/or 16420, the court is not persuaded by the Motion's arguments. Probate Code sections 15642 (Removal of Trustee), 16060-16064 (Trustee's Duty to Report Information and Account to Beneficiaries), and 16420 (Breach of Trust) concern the duties and liabilities of trustees to beneficiaries. The court does not find these statutes relevant to deciding the Motion as presented. Petitioners are not claiming to be either beneficiaries or trustees, but instead to be judgment creditors of the Trust and Estate and interested parties as defined under Probate Code section 48. On the face of the Petition, the court finds Petitioners appear to be "interested parties" as defined under Probate Code section 48, with an interest in both the Estate and Trust as judgment creditors of Decedent. Insofar as the Motion is brought pursuant to Probate Code section 17202, that section states in its entirety, "The court may dismiss a petition if it appears that the proceeding is not reasonably necessary for the protection of the interests of the trustee or beneficiary." The court's power to dismiss a petition under this statute is discretionary and not mandatory. The court declines the Motion's request to dismiss the Petition on this basis, at this time. Further, the court is not entirely convinced, by the Motion or from the face of the Petition, that the Petition's remaining causes of action contain a claim regarding the "internal affairs" of the Trust under Probate Code sec. 17200(b), or specifically sub(b)(20), as the Motion argues. Petitioners, alleging they are judgment creditors of both the Trust and Estate, appear to be seeking relief on the basis of other legal theories. As recently discussed in Hamlin v. Jendayi (2024) 105 Cal. App. 5th 1064, 1075, Section 17200 contains no language purporting to limit standing only to trustees and beneficiaries of a trust or otherwise indicating the Legislature's intent to exclude others from contesting a trust in the probate court. Rather, the statute simply provides that trustees and trust beneficiaries "may" petition the court under this chapter "[e]xcept" as provided in section 15800-i.e., during the time the trust remains revocable, when joint action of settlor and beneficiaries is required, or "to the extent that the trust instrument otherwise provides." ([sec.] 17200, subd. (a), citing [sec.] 15800.) But the mere use of the words "trustee or beneficiary" is hardly an indication of a legislative intent to circumscribe the probate court's power to confer standing to contest a trust on persons other than trustees and trust beneficiaries.

rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE ANTONIA DUGAN 2005 TRUST,DATED JUNE 29, 2005, AS RESTATED ON DECEMBER 9, 2022
rulings.Calendar Matter: Petition For Modification Of Trust Probate Code 15409, 17200
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. The judicial officer is to review and determine whether the proposed trust modification should be approved, to the extent the petition relies on statutory modification under Probate Code section 15409, in the absence of supporting declarations from the drafting attorney or other witnesses having first-hand knowledge of the circumstances leading up to the execution of the December 2022 trust restatement. The petition alleges that the settlor "had no reason to anticipate that Paul (beneficiary) would later require Medi-Cal", but the supplement alleges that the settlor "intended to protect those (Medi-Cal) benefits", while disclosing petitioner's lack of knowledge as to when the beneficiary started to receive Medi-Cal benefits. It should also be noted that paragraph 3(B)(6) of the trust gives the trustee an option to terminate the beneficiary's share of the trust and distribute everything to petitioner with a precatory request to use the distributed assets for the beneficiary, in the event that the beneficiary becomes ineligible for SSI and Medi-Cal benefits. The judicial officer is also to review and determine whether the proposed trust modification should be approved, to the extent the petition relies on common law modification based on peculiar or exceptional circumstances. No evidence has been submitted to prove the settlor's intent not to impose any obligation on the trustee to consider other sources of support and take whatever steps that may be necessary under paragraph 3(B)(3) of the trust. While the first sentence of the end of paragraph 3(B)(4) of the trust provides for the trustee's authority to pay for the beneficiary's support or maintenance if independent or semi-independent living is appropriate for the beneficiary, the supplement admits that such independent or semi-independent living is not probable for the beneficiary (in which case the trustee's authority to pay for the beneficiary's support or maintenance does not appear to come into play). The second sentence of the end of paragraph 3(B)(4) of the trust providing for the trustee's authority to permit the beneficiary to occupy any home that may become an asset of the trust is also sought to be deleted, but a home is not a countable resource that would affect the beneficiary's eligibility for SSI or Medi-Cal benefits.
